# Emergency screen — labeled cases (synthetic)

Validation set for `rules.emergency_signal()` and for the model's `emergency` intent.  All texts are invented; no real patient.

**Set A is not populated in this file.**

**Set B — generated by Claude (Fable 5.1), Sept 23, 2026, from a list of situations (who texts this number and why).**  Caveat: the author had read the regex, so these lean toward phrasings it does not contain.  Treat as a stress set, not a base rate.  Kate to review labels; disputed rows get a note.

**Set B result, code floor only (`emergency_signal`), Sept 23:** 55 cases, 30 E / 25 N.  Sensitivity 4/30 = 13%.  Specificity 19/25 = 76%.  The model layer (`emergency` intent) has not been run on this set.  The six false alarms are all past events, a pet, a TV show, and "911 operator training."


**Live run, Sept 23, 2026, 12:47–14:18 (Opus 5, `eval/run_emergency_eval.py --adapter anthropic`, cap $0.50):** **all 55 calls failed** with `api status 400: Schema is too complex`.  $0.00 billed; the 90 minutes was retry backoff.  `INTENT_SCHEMA` in `ocp/llm/base.py` was last changed Sept 16 (v4 build, v4 reconcile, v5 build — 1,542 chars, 84 nodes, 20-value intent enum, planner actions); the last successful live run was Sept 15 on the smaller schema.  This run produced no successful live classifications.  Current live-classifier operation remains unverified.  The engine has a model-unavailable fallback (`_model_unavailable_exit`); this evaluation does not establish its clinical safety.  Open: investigate the schema rejection and record a successful live classification run before describing the live classifier as working.  Results JSON: `eval/results/emergency-claude-opus-5-20260923T141800.json` (not included in this portfolio).
